changelog: THE BATTLEFIELD NOW WORKS LIKE A CAMERA. Scroll to pan, ctrl-scroll to zoom, and +, - or 0 from the keyboard — zooming holds the point under your cursor instead of jumping to the middle, and panning stops at the edge of the table rather than drifting off into nothing. THE BOARD FITS THE WINDOW AGAIN: a battle opens with the whole battlefield visible and nothing to scroll to, and scrolling only appears once you have zoomed in. THE REPLAY FOLLOWS THE FIGHT — when a shot is fired at ground you can see but are not looking at, the camera moves there first and then plays it, so you watch the hit land instead of finding the aftermath; anything in fog is left alone. THE DAILY COMMISSION IS A DIFFERENT GAME EVERY DAY. Alongside the day's commander and modifiers it now deals two starting exceptions — one for the force that marches out, one for the kit it carries. An armoured column with no infantry. A skeleton crew and the salvage to fix that. Two curses from the first step. A relic, and the price of carrying it. Every reinforcement order rescinded. Sixteen in all, two per day, the same for everyone, and named on the menu so you can see what you are walking into before you spend the run. A LOST COMMISSION NOW SCORES: the day is banked whether you clear it or not, because how far you got is the whole point of a shared seed. THE GAME EXPLAINS ITSELF AT THE MOMENT IT MATTERS. Coaching used to wait until a panel closed, so the tip telling you what a card draft costs arrived once the draft was gone. Every one of those now lands while the choice is still in front of you. The Nomad's Momentum gets a tip of its own — it banks a compounding amount at end of turn, climbs when the whole column moves and halves when one unit stands still, and none of that was written down anywhere you could read it. FIXED: the sluggishness during play; commander portraits and their doctrine text vanishing from the Generals page after scrolling; Settings opening behind the Generals panel; the top bar overlapping itself and slicing labels in half in a smaller window; the menu title flickering as the pointer crossed the buttons; buttons that responded four different ways to a hover; and the Drive meter that read "climbs to 0, halves to 0" on every turn until your last unit had moved.
